newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Lukoil says oil reserves 10.7 bln barrels.
newsitem.headline: Russian Lukoil says oil reserves 10.7 bln barrels.

text.p: Russia's NK LUKoil said in a statement on Monday that its total proven oil reserves in Russia were 10.7 billion barrels based on an audit by U.S. engineers Miller & Lents.

LUKoil said that a previous Miller & Lents audit did not include reserves in the European part of Russia, and said that the new total made LUKoil the world's single largest oil company in terms of proven reserves.
Miller and Lents, in an audit released by LUKoil in March 1996, put the company's proven reserves at 10.50 billion barrels.
The Monday statement gave no information on the degrees to which the total reserves were commercially recoverable.
It said that the addition to the 1996 figure came from LUKoil units LUKoil-Permneft, LUKoil-Nizhnevolzhskneft, LUKoil-Kaliningradmorneft and LUKoil-Astrakhanneft.

Total oil reserves at those three companies were 3.18 billion barrels, of which 2.85 billion barrels were commercially recoverable. It said that the three companies had gas reserves of 1.09 trillion cubic feet.
The statement said LUKoil would also have an audit of its reserves outside Russia and would re-audit reserves annually.
LUKoil said in January that according to preliminary figures it produced 58.3 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, slightly above 1995's 57.3 million tonnes.
It planned 1997 output rising to 59.7 million tonnes.
